objective: Standard statement: let T be a cubic signed system with a Pfaffian signing that is the trisum of three pieces P1, P2, P3 along a square C = (c0, c1, c2, c3) (c0, c2 points, c1, c3 lines; the square's edges deleted); give each piece its square edges back with a Pfaffian signing; the leaning split (alpha_i, beta_i) of P_i counts (halved) the colourings of P_i - c1 by whether the free point of c3 agrees, as seen by c3, with c0 or with c2; (1) seen from c3 the split is (beta_i, alpha_i), and reversing a piece's orientation swaps alpha_i and beta_i; (2) the trisum law: a(T) = rho1 rho2 rho3 - alpha1 alpha2 alpha3 - beta1 beta2 beta3 with rho_i = alpha_i + beta_i the piece amplitudes; that is, not-all-equal on the leanings of the three pieces; (3) a piece glued to two others at a square receives from them the weights rho_Q rho_R - alpha_Q alpha_R and rho_Q rho_R - beta_Q beta_R on its own two leanings at that square, with the roles exchanged on the other square line. Nearest known result: Robertson-Seymour-Thomas trisums; THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE-20261030-001A and C. Classification: to be decided.
status: Proved: the trisum law A(T) = rho1 rho2 rho3 - alpha1 alpha2 alpha3 - beta1 beta2 beta3 (not-all-equal on the pieces' leanings); support lemma; the other view is the swapped split; children act as weights on a piece's two leanings
title: The trisum law
